headline: Growth broadens across segments; guidance reaffirmed

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based: Healthcare +8% on consumables/services share gains and capital-equipment order growth, AST +6% on price, Life Sciences +9% on capital equipment and price/volume.

Segment gains were driven by improved volume, price, productivity and favorable mix (Healthcare), price (AST), and price/volume (Life Sciences), partly offset by inflation, tariffs, depreciation and labor costs.
Net income growth trails operating income growth, reflecting a higher effective tax rate (26.5% vs 23.3% a year ago) on the pretax income gain.
EPS growth (+14.0%) modestly exceeds net income growth (+12.8%) due to a smaller diluted share count (97.9M vs 98.8M) from ongoing buybacks.
Adjusted EPS excludes intangible amortization ($65.3M) and other items per the non-GAAP reconciliation table; the exclusions were similar in size to the prior-year quarter.
Decline versus the prior year reflects a much smaller working-capital contribution this quarter, partly offset by higher net income.
Tracks the same weaker working-capital contribution cited for operating cash flow, partly offset by higher net income.
Cash rose q/q as $367.1M of operating inflows exceeded $108.5M of investing and $213.5M of financing outflows (including $115.5M buybacks, $61.4M dividends), netting to a $42.8M increase.
Long-term debt fell q/q partly reflecting a $124.5M shift into short-term indebtedness, which rose by roughly the same amount; the release does not explain the mix shift.

CEO Dan Carestio cited "stable underlying demand," with consumables/services share gains and solid capital-equipment order growth; the company also announced a targeted restructuring plan for a new North Carolina chemistries facility.

summary_short: STERIS revenue grew 7.3% y/y to $1,492.7M (6% organic) in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, with diluted EPS up 14.0% to $2.04 and adjusted diluted EPS up 10.7% to $2.59; the company reaffirmed FY2027 revenue/EPS guidance while raising planned capex and trimming its free-cash-flow outlook.
summary_long: Revenue rose 7% y/y (6% organic) to $1,492.7M, led by Healthcare (+8%, consumables/services share gains, capital-equipment order growth), with AST +6% and Life Sciences +9%. Operating income grew 16% to $285.8M on volume, price, productivity and mix, offset by inflation and tariffs. Net income rose 13% to $200.1M; diluted EPS $2.04 (+14%), adjusted EPS $2.59 (+11%). Operating cash flow fell 13% to $367.1M and free cash flow fell 14% to $279.6M on weaker working-capital contribution. Cash rose to $482.3M; long-term debt fell to $1,650.2M. STERIS reaffirmed FY2027 revenue (7-8%), organic growth (6-7%) and adjusted EPS ($11.10-$11.30) guidance, raised planned capex to ~$450M (from $375M) for a new North Carolina facility, and lowered free-cash-flow outlook to ~$800M (from $850M).
